The map's label for the Hindu Buddhist kingdoms of eastern Java, centred on the Brantas river valley, shown from 1000 to 1200. In 929 king Mpu Sindok moved the court of Mataram from central Java to the east. Why is not clear; a volcanic eruption and war are both suggested.

In 1016 the court was destroyed in an attack. The young prince Airlangga escaped and rebuilt the kingdom, called Kahuripan. Before his death in 1049 he split it in two: Janggala and Kediri. Kediri became the stronger. Its court poets wrote long Old Javanese poems based on the Indian epics, and its ports traded rice and spices with Srivijaya and China.

In 1222 Ken Arok defeated Kediri and founded Singhasari, which led in turn to Majapahit.
